Work weightwise, with finitely many sequences. For each unordered pair choose one orientation and set P_ij=Q_ij, P_ji=1. The other factorizations are homogeneous too: in a positively weighted polynomial domain, the extreme weighted degrees of a product cannot cancel, so a homogeneous nonzero product has homogeneous factors. Define the shift of a sequence by a sum over its ordered unequal-colour pairs; exchanging neighboring i,j changes that sum by Delta_ij=-b_ij-deg P_ij. The factorization gives Delta_ji=-Delta_ij, so assigning one half of this pair function in either orientation integrates the increments (without dividing by 2). Equal-colour increments vanish. This proves the claimed homogeneous action and uniqueness on each weight orbit.
For relations, multiplication and permutations verify (1)-(3), far crossings verify (5), and partial_a=(1-s_a)/(x_a-x_(a+1)) satisfies partial_a x_a-x_(a+1)partial_a=1, partial_a x_(a+1)-x_a partial_a=-1 and partial_a^2=0 by applying both sides to an arbitrary polynomial. On an unequal-colour component the two consecutive crossings multiply by P_ji(x_(a+1),x_a)P_ij(x_a,x_(a+1))=Q_ij(x_a,x_(a+1)), proving (4). For (7), three distinct colours give the same product of the three pair factors times the longest permutation. Three equal colours give the common operator sum_(w in S3)sgn(w)w divided by (x_a-x_(a+1))(x_a-x_(a+2))(x_(a+1)-x_(a+2)). The cases with only the first or last two colours equal follow from partial_a(fg)=partial_a(f)g+s_a(f)partial_a(g); the case (i,j,i) gives exactly (Q_ij(x_a,x_(a+1))-Q_ij(x_(a+2),x_(a+1)))/(x_(a+2)-x_a). Thus all relations hold with the already fixed native sign.
For independence, pass only for this argument to the direct sum of rational function fields. Each chosen reduced crossing word has a nonzero coefficient times its permutation, plus terms of strictly smaller permutation length: unequal crossings contribute their nonzero P-factor and equal crossings contribute the nonzero reflection coefficient of partial_a. Distinct field automorphisms are linearly independent over the field: from a shortest purported relation sum c_w w=0, evaluate on fg and subtract one selected w(g) times its evaluation on f; choosing g separated by two different permutations produces a shorter relation, a contradiction. The same argument in each source/destination idempotent block separates its permutation operators. Hence the PBW spanning monomials are independent under this action and the representation is faithful; this is not inferred merely from surjectivity after localization. Once the P-factors and equal-colour differences are inverted, unequal crossings give s_a and equal crossings give s_a=1-(x_a-x_(a+1))partial_a. These generate the skew group algebra, proving precisely the localized isomorphism. Finiteness of each homogeneous component is weightwise and follows from the PBW finite crossing words and positive dot degrees, not from a finite total-dimensional algebra. No AC is used.

Use far commutations and braid moves to turn a nonreduced permutation word into one with an adjacent repeated simple reflection, then use (4) to remove that pair. Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta,\gamma\in Q_+$.
(i) **Freeness.** $1_{\beta,\gamma}R(\beta+\gamma):=e(\beta,\gamma)R(\beta+\gamma)$ is a free graded left $R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)$-module with basis $\{\widetilde w\}$ indexed by the minimal length representatives $w$ of the left cosets of $S_{|\beta|}\times S_{|\gamma|}$ in $S_{|\beta|+|\gamma|}$, each $\widetilde w$ a sum of staircase diagrams over the words of $\beta,\gamma$; its rank is $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$.
(ii) **Exactness.** $\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}$ and $\mathrm{Res}_{\beta,\gamma}$ are exact functors between the graded module categories.
(iii) **Frobenius reciprocity.** $\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{Res}_{\beta,\gamma}$: there is a natural degree-zero bijection $\mathrm{Hom}_{R(\beta+\gamma)}(\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N),L)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{R(\beta)\otimes R(\gamma)}(M\boxtimes N,\mathrm{Res}_{\beta,\gamma}L)$.
(iv) **Biadjunction.** $\mathrm{Res}_{\beta,\gamma}$ is also left adjoint to $\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}$; the unit and counit are the cup and cap diagrams built from the closing-diagram trace $t$ on $R(\beta+\gamma)$ of the Frobenius form over the center, and are compatible with the grading up to the shifts recorded in $t$. Here $t$ is the degree-normalized linear form on $R(\beta+\gamma)$ given on the PBW basis by the coefficient of the longest word $w_0$ (the closing-diagram functional), with the scalar normalization adjusted on the two-colour crossings so that it is symmetrizing; the exact normalization is pinned at authoring against KL §2.2 and Webster §1.3.
(v) **Projectives.** $\mathrm{Res}_{\beta,\gamma}$ and $\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}$ carry finite graded projective modules to finite graded projective modules.
All assertions are functorial in $M,N,L$ and compatible with the grading shifts of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]].
edits.after:
Let Q be the KLR datum above and beta,gamma in Q_+. Put A=R(beta+gamma), B=R(beta) tensor_k R(gamma), e=e(beta,gamma), and c=(beta|gamma). The bimodules eA and Ae are finite graded free respectively as left and right B-modules, with labelled minimal-shuffle bases and binomial(|beta|+|gamma|,|beta|) basis elements. Ind=Ae tensor_B - and Res=e(-) are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. Ind is left adjoint to Res. The right adjoint of Res is Coind=HOM_B(eA,-), with (a f)(t)=f(ta), and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
Coind_(beta,gamma)(M boxtimes N) ~= Ind_(gamma,beta)(N boxtimes M){c}.
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded B-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic E_i/F_i biadjunction theorem.

edits.before: Follow the sources in order. (i) is KL I Proposition 2.16 with its explicit basis of staircases and the coset count; the same basis is displayed in KK Corollary 3.4's decomposition. (ii) $\mathrm{Res}$ is exact because idempotent multiplication is exact; $\mathrm{Ind}$ is exact by the HA-18 tensor exactness theorem applied to the kernel $R(\beta+\gamma)e(\beta,\gamma)$, which is flat as a right $R(\beta)\otimes R(\gamma)$-module because it is free by (i). (iii) is the standard adjunction of $M\mapsto Ae\otimes_BM$ and $N\mapsto eN$ for a ring inclusion $B\hookrightarrow A$ with $e$ idempotent (KL I §2.6, opening paragraph; KK (3.12)) reformulated in the graded setting via the HA-18 tensor-Hom adjunction. (iv) The closing-diagram functional is well defined and homogeneous on the PBW basis of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]; cyclicity $t(ab)=t(ba)$ is checked on the two-colour crossings with the adjusted scalar so that the result is symmetric (Webster §1.3, Theorem 1.8 and Remark 1.9, in the generic/idempotent-corner form), and Rouquier §2.3.2 supplies the equivalence between a Frobenius form and an adjunction of the extension/restriction pair; this produces the natural bijections $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathrm{Res}L,M)\cong\mathrm{Hom}(L,\mathrm{Ind}M)$ and the compatible cup/cap morphisms. (v) For $\mathrm{Res}$: if $P$ is a degree-zero summand of a finite sum of shifts of $R(\beta+\gamma)$, then $\mathrm{Res}P$ is a degree-zero summand of a finite sum of shifts of $1_{\beta,\gamma}R(\beta+\gamma)$, which is free, hence projective, by (i) and HA-18's projective-preservation theorem (KL I Corollary 2.17). For $\mathrm{Ind}$: it is a left adjoint of the exact $\mathrm{Res}$ by (iii), and a left adjoint of an exact functor carries projectives to projectives; or, directly, HA-18's tensor theorem applies since $R(\beta+\gamma)e(\beta,\gamma)$ is finite graded projective as a left $R(\beta+\gamma)$-module. No AC is used beyond the ambient module-category arguments, which are choice-free at this size.
edits.after:
Choose minimal shuffle representatives and fixed reduced words. Every permutation has a unique parabolic-times-minimal-shuffle decomposition with additive length, so the PBW basis identifies eA with a finite direct sum of shifts of B as a left module, and horizontal reflection gives Ae as a right module. This proves both freeness claims. Idempotent multiplication is exact and tensor with a free right module is exact; projective summands of finite shifted free modules stay projective under restriction by the first freeness claim and under induction because Ae is a projective left A-module. The balanced map a tensor m -> (l -> appropriate image) or directly the universal property of tensor gives Hom_A(Ae tensor_B X,L)=Hom_B(X,eL). The right-adjoint bijection is Hom_B(eL,X)=Hom_A(L,HOM_B(eA,X)), with maps f -> (l -> (t -> f(tl))) and g -> (el -> g(l)(e)); these are inverse and preserve degree.
For the second-adjunction bimodule, let y be the longest block shuffle, of degree -c, and e'=e(gamma,beta). Use PBW to project eAe' to its y coefficient, interpreted in B by identifying the reversed blocks. Denote this B-balanced coefficient map by t. Dot slides and block crossing slides preserve the longest-shuffle coefficient; all dot/braid correction terms have shorter shuffle length and vanish under t. Thus t is balanced for the block-flip equivalence. The map Ae' -> HOM_B(eA,B), z -> (u -> t(uz)), has degree c. Pair the left and right shuffle bases by complementary shuffles. Ordered by shuffle length, their coefficient matrix is triangular with diagonal units 1 (equal-colour signs are absorbed in the reflected chosen words); to see this, a complementary pair is the reduced longest shuffle and every noncomplementary pair either misses its permutation or reduces by a quadratic/braid correction to smaller length. Finite triangular elimination gives an inverse over B, without localization or a central Frobenius trace. Hence HOM_B(eA,B) ~= Ae'{c} with the right B action transported by block flip. Since eA is finite free over B, evaluation identifies HOM_B(eA,B) tensor_B X with HOM_B(eA,X). This proves the functorial formula on all graded modules. The longest-shuffle functional and the triangular basis calculation are the local content of Lauda-Vazirani Theorem2.2/§2.3, read on the full source, translated to the fixed native sign and the actual homogeneous-Hom convention. No cyclotomic trace is imported and no AC is used.

That proof imports: quiver flag varieties and proper maps; equivariant constructible and perverse derived categories; Verdier duality and the decomposition theorem/semisimplicity of the Lusztig complexes; equivariant Ext and Borel-Moore homology/convolution; equivariant formality and base change; and Lusztig's perverse-sheaf canonical-basis theorem. None of these foundations has an authored supplier in this library, and no published or drafted item supplies them. The alternative nongeometric sources known to the scaffolder are: Brundan-Kleshchev, Graded decomposition numbers for cyclotomic Hecke algebras, Theorem 5.19 (affine type $A$ cyclotomic, characteristic $0$, via Ariki's theorem), summarized as Kleshchev §9.1 Theorem 9.2; and Rouquier's announced general result. The first is a cyclotomic statement and does not directly give the generic symmetric-type statement (nor is Ariki's theorem available locally); the second is an announcement, not a proof. The scaffold therefore records the item as escalated with the exact missing input: either (a) register and build the displayed geometric supplier stack, or (b) supply a complete nongeometric proof of the generic symmetric characteristic-zero statement. The statement itself, the dependency interfaces and the normalization conventions are as displayed and are not weakened.
edits.after:
Held on the precise geometric foundations, with the full symmetric/characteristic-zero/loopless-quiver scope preserved, including multiple edges (VV§1.1 and Remark3.3(b)). The proof must construct delta L=sum_i (pi_i)!k[dim Ftilde_i] on E_V and prove R(beta)=Ext_G^*(delta L,delta L) in the fixed graded/sign convention (VVTheorem3.6). Proper pushforward semisimplicity is essential, not a definition: prove the needed Decomposition Theorem for these quiver flag maps. Ext/convolution comparison and equivariant localization/formality/base change must be proved locally or supplied by proved local prerequisites; VV Lemma1.8(b), Lemma2.18, Lemma2.27 and Lemma4.8/§4.10 explicitly import them.
Conditional on that foundation, the final algebraic argument is complete: write delta L=sum_(S,r) M_(S,r) tensor S[r] over simple perverse summands S. Then Y_S=Ext_G^*(delta L,S) is a projective summand of the regular Ext-module. Central augmentation and formality identify its reduction with Ext^*(delta L,S). After shifting the multiplicity spaces, the auxiliary Ext-degree grading is nonnegative, with degree-zero ring product_S End(M_S); negative Ext between perverse sheaves vanishes and Hom(S,T)=delta_(S,T)k. Its positive ideal is nilpotent and Y_S has degree-zero part M_S generating it, hence its unique simple head is M_S. Thus Y_S is indecomposable. Every projective summand is represented because delta L contains all S; the normalized Y_S give all shift orbits. Word complexes map to word projectives, so their Grothendieck map equals gamma on the integral half (torsionfree descent from the field word span).
A separate GENERAL-symmetric bridge must identify these normalized sheaf classes with the Kashiwara lower global vectors. The existing QG5 canonical-comparison supplier is explicitly finite ADE and is not this proof. Prove the geometric form norm/congruence, Verdier bar and actual restriction/divided-string leading coefficient +1; use B_L=C_nu B_K, C_nu=1 mod q, and the general integral balanced uniqueness supplier. Norm1 gives only a signed global set; the positive string recursion from1 is required to remove the signs. The based quotient then follows from the general QG5 zero/survival theorem. No source citation, finite-ADE restriction, bare K_0 isomorphism or right-module twist substitutes for these missing foundations.

(a) The algebra R(alpha_i+alpha_j) has the PBW basis displayed below even for Q=0. Indeed dots slide past crossings and crossing squares vanish, so those monomials span; independence follows from the algebra of the two-idempotent polynomial skew quiver with both length-two crossing paths zero. There is no factorization with both factors nonzero, since k[u,v] is a domain.
(b) Taking P_ij=0 and P_ji=1 gives a well-defined polynomial action: tau_1 kills the ij summand and swaps the ji summand into ij. Hence it kills the NONZERO element tau_1 e(ij), so is not faithful; it need not kill both crossings. For any polynomial-factor action with Q=0 at least one crossing factor vanishes, giving the same nonfaithfulness conclusion in that corner.

edits.after: (a) Define the degenerate algebra as the direct sum of the two polynomial identity corners and the two polynomial crossing arrows, with dot permutation on crossing multiplication and products of two arrows zero. Associativity follows because the permutation is an algebra automorphism and every triple with at least two arrows is zero. This realizes exactly the presentation and proves PBW independence without applying the nondegenerate PBW theorem outside its hypotheses. (b) A product of polynomial factors is zero only if at least one is zero. With P_ij=0,P_ji=1 the polynomial action kills tau_1e(ij) but not tau_1e(ji); both algebra elements are nonzero by (a). Hence this action is not faithful. The same argument applies to every factorized action since one corner is killed.
